statement: Greshko’s fixed v2 tables preserved normalized letter streams on both independent texts. A position-dependent homophone choice raised paragraph-initial p/f enrichment to 2.68–3.94 times mid-line frequency in six runs. All six fell below F-003’s tenfold criterion and F-008’s threefold first-line criterion. The joint positional question remains open.
citation: Michael A. Greshko (2025), The Naibbe cipher, Cryptologia, doi:10.1080/01611194.2025.2566408.
methods: Use naibbe_v2.py from the linked revision, the published 78-card deck and tables, RESPACING=17, UNAMBIGUOUS=True. Use the output before optional space removal. Use only the first 32,000 letters from clean_line applied to joined vs.refcorpus.blocks_of of each pin. Encrypt the entire stream in one call, with Python random seeds 0, 1, 2. Pack ciphertext into eight tokens per line, four lines per paragraph. Include the final partial paragraph. This artificial layout is independent of the source punctuation.

Freeze a second layout rule using the same baseline tokens. Form the set of possible plaintexts for each ciphertext from all unigram assignments and all concatenated prefix/suffix assignments. Keep, for each plaintext, the lexicographically ordered p/f-initial ciphertext alternatives for which that unrestricted set is a singleton. For each token in order, skip unless it has alternatives and starts with neither p nor f. Draw from random.Random(1000+seed). Replace uniformly from its alternatives with probability 1 at a paragraph opening, 1/3 elsewhere on a paragraph’s first line, 1/8 at a subsequent line opening, and 0 elsewhere. This explicitly imposes a positional preference.

For round trips, the fixed generator disallows every bigram spelling colliding with a unigram or with any other prefix/suffix code pair. Compare every produced token’s admissible singleton with the recorded plaintext token, and compare their concatenation with the normalized input. Raw table ambiguity counts all parses without these generator restrictions. No claim is made for punctuation, original word breaks, or optional further space deletion.

Count initial EVA p/f at paragraph openings versus non-edge words, at line openings versus non-edge words, and throughout first lines versus subsequent lines. Count EVA-basic glyphs for lengths and first-order conditional glyph entropy in bits per transition with a shared boundary symbol at both edges of each token. Type counts use whole ciphertext tokens. F-003 and F-008 supply the preregistered comparison thresholds from the public record. These are synthetic tests, with no search against manuscript pages.
